function.name: edit_file

function.name: exec
function.description:
Executes shell commands with PicoClaw's configured safety guards.

Be aware: OS: linux, Shell: sh

All commands run in the configured working directory by default. Use the cwd parameter to select another directory; do not use cd to change directories inside a command.

IMPORTANT: Use this tool for terminal operations such as git, go, npm, and docker. For listing, searching, reading, or editing files, use PicoClaw's filesystem tools (list_dir, search_files, read_file, edit_file, append_file, and write_file) when available.

Before a command explicitly creates files or directories, use list_dir when available to verify that the parent exists and is the intended location. Always quote paths containing spaces. Command output is returned by the tool.

Usage notes:
- action is required; command is required for action=run.
- The optional timeout parameter is in seconds and overrides the configured timeout for foreground commands; 0 disables the timeout. It cannot be combined with background=true. Foreground output longer than the configured limit (default 50,000 chars) is truncated to the first 40% and last 60% around an omission notice; background session output is limited to 1 MB.
- Use background=true for long-running commands. The result includes a sessionId. Use action=list to list sessions; use poll, wait, read, write, send-keys, or kill with sessionId to manage one. poll returns immediately; to wait for a session to finish use wait instead of polling in a loop. write sends stdin; send-keys sends keys to a PTY. Sessions are cleaned up 30 minutes after the process exits.
- Combine background=true with pty=true for interactive sessions when supported. PTY is not supported on Windows.
- Run independent commands in separate tool calls. If commands depend on each other, chain them with && so a failure stops the sequence. Use semicolons only when later commands may run even if an earlier one fails. Do not use newlines to separate commands; newlines inside quoted strings are fine.

action.description: Action: run (execute command), list (show sessions), poll (check status, returns immediately), wait (block until a session exits or timeout), read (get output), write (send input), kill (terminate), send-keys (send keys to PTY)

command.description: Shell command to execute (required for run)

data.description: Data to write to stdin (required for write)

keys.description: Key names for send-keys: up, down, left, right, enter, tab, escape, backspace, ctrl-c, ctrl-d, home, end, pageup, pagedown, f1-f12

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal (PTY) when available

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds for foreground commands; overrides the configured timeout, and 0 disables the timeout. Not supported with background=true. For wait: maximum seconds to block (default and cap: the configured timeout).

function.name: find_skills
function.description: Search for installable skills from skill registries. Returns skill slugs, descriptions, versions, and relevance scores. Use this to discover skills before installing them with install_skill.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20, default 5)

query.description: Search query describing the desired skill capability (e.g., 'github integration', 'database management')

function.name: install_skill
function.description: Install a skill from a registry by slug. Defaults to GitHub when registry is omitted. Downloads and extracts the skill into the workspace. Use find_skills first to discover available skills.

force.description: Force reinstall if skill already exists (default false)

registry.description: Registry to install from (optional, defaults to 'github')

slug.description: The unique slug of the skill to install (e.g., 'github', 'docker-compose')

version.description: Specific version to install (optional, defaults to latest)

function.name: list_dir
function.description: List files and directories in a path

function.name: load_image
function.description: Load a local image file so you can analyze its contents with vision. Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP. After calling this tool, describe or analyze the image in your next response.

path.description: Path to the local image file. Relative paths are resolved from workspace.

function.name: message
function.description: Send a text message to the user on a chat channel.

content.description: Optional message text. When media is present, this text is used as the caption/body for the media message.

reply_to_message_id.description: Optional: reply target message ID for channels that support threaded replies

function.name: reaction
function.description: Add a reaction to a message. Defaults to the current inbound message when message_id is omitted.

message_id.description: Optional: target message ID; defaults to the current inbound message

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports pagination via `offset` and `length`.

length.description: Maximum number of bytes to read.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading from.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. target='content' does regex search with files_only, count, or context output; target='files' finds names by glob or substring (an empty pattern lists files). Skipped: paths ignored by .gitignore/.ignore or .git, and binary files (NUL byte in the first 8 KiB); other encodings are searched. Credential-looking tokens in results are replaced with [FILTERED]. Supports pagination. On macOS, searches above your home directory skip TCC-protected folders; target one directly to include it. Searches the configured readable filesystem sandbox.

context.description: Lines before and after each content match (maximum: 20); contiguous matches merge into one block

file_glob.description: Optional filename pattern for content search (same syntax as pattern for target=files)

offset.description: Number of results to skip (results are match lines, or merged context blocks when context > 0)

order.description: File search order; modified sorts by newest modification time and scans the full tree

pattern.description: Regex for content search (empty matches every line), or a filename pattern for target=files: a glob such as *.go, src/**/*.ts or *.{js,ts}, or a plain substring such as docker-compose (empty lists every file)

function.name: send_file
function.description: Send a local file (image, document, etc.) to the user on the current chat channel.

filename.description: Optional display filename. Defaults to the basename of path.

path.description: Path to the local file. Relative paths are resolved from workspace.

function.name: spawn
function.description: Spawn a subagent to handle a task in the background. Use this for complex or time-consuming tasks that can run independently. Call it several times in one step to run subagents in parallel. The result arrives automatically when the subagent is done; never poll or sleep to wait for it.

agent_id.description: Optional target agent ID to delegate the task to

label.description: Optional short label for the task (for display)

task.description: The task for subagent to complete

function.name: subagent
function.description: Execute a subagent task synchronously and return the result. Use this for delegating specific tasks to an independent agent instance. Returns execution summary to user and full details to LLM.

label.description: Optional short label for the task (for display)

task.description: The task for subagent to complete

function.name: todo
function.description:
Create and maintain a structured task list for the current session. Tracks progress and surfaces status to the user.

Each write replaces the whole list: always send every item, including unchanged ones, with a stable unique id. Use `read` before resuming or after context loss; never rewrite a plan from memory.

## When to use
- Task has 3+ distinct steps, spans multiple files, or the user listed several tasks or asked for a todo list.
- New user instructions mid-session: add them as items before starting.
- Several tool calls for one conceptual step do not count as separate steps.

## When NOT to use
- Single action or fewer than 3 trivial steps.
- Informational or conversational requests.

## States
- `pending`: not started.
- `in_progress`: working on it. At most one at a time; a write with more than one is rejected.
- `completed`: done AND verified.
- `canceled`: no longer needed. Cancel instead of deleting.

## Priority
`high` (blocks other work or user-critical), `medium` (default if omitted), `low` (optional, cleanup).

## Rules
- Mark `completed` right after finishing, not in batches.
- Mark `completed` only after verification passes (tests, build, confirmed change). If it fails or was not run, keep it `in_progress` or add a fix item.
- If blocked: keep the item `in_progress`, add a `pending` item naming the blocker, and tell the user what is needed.
- Follow-ups found during work: add as new `pending` items.
- Content: specific, imperative, in the user's language. "Add dark mode toggle to Settings", not "Dark mode".
- Keep commands, flags, paths, and identifiers verbatim (e.g. `go test ./... -race`).
- Plan, not log: do not add an item per tool call.
- Clear an obsolete plan with `todos: []`.

## Limits
Max 100 items; content up to 1024 bytes; id up to 128 bytes. Plans live in memory for the session only: lost on restart, cleared with the conversation. This tool does not execute or schedule tasks.

## Examples
- "Add a dark mode toggle and run the tests" -> feature items + explicit test item.
- "Rename getCwd across the repo" (15 hits in 8 files) -> rename item + verification item.
- "How do I print Hello World?", "Add a comment to calculateTotal", "Run npm install" -> skip.

todos.description: Required for write: the full replacement list. An empty array clears it.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch a URL and extract readable content (HTML to text). Use this to get weather info, news, articles, or any web content.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for current information. Supports query, count, and an optional temporal range filter. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets from search results.

range.description: Optional time filter: d (day), w (week), m (month), y (year)

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, replacing any existing content. Content is written byte-for-byte after argument decoding. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for a literal backslash-n sequence. If the file already exists you must set overwrite=true, which replaces the ENTIRE file. To add to or change part of an existing file without losing its current contents, use append_file or edit_file instead.

content.description: Content to write to the file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for literal backslash-n.

overwrite.description: Set to true to replace an existing file in full. This discards the file's current contents — to preserve them, use append_file or edit_file instead of write_file.

path.description: Path to the file to write

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command and return its output. Commands run with DeepClaw's configured execution isolation, safety guards, timeout and output limits. Use read, write and edit for file operations. Chain dependent commands with &&; use the cwd parameter instead of cd. A simpler interface does not make arbitrary commands safe.

cwd.description: Optional working directory, relative to the workspace or an allowed path.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds; 0 disables the timeout.

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a file by replacing one exact, unique occurrence of old_text with new_text. Read the file first if you need to confirm its current content.

new_text.description: The text to replace with. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for literal backslash-n.

old_text.description: The exact text to find and replace. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for literal backslash-n.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file from the workspace. Use offset and length to read part of a large file.

length.description: Maximum number of bytes to read.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading from.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. By default an existing file is not replaced; set overwrite=true to replace the whole file. Use edit for targeted changes that must preserve the rest of the file.

content.description: Content to write to the file. Standard JSON escaping applies: \n for newline and \\n for literal backslash-n.

overwrite.description: Set to true to replace an existing file in full. This discards the file's current contents — to preserve them, use edit instead of write.

path.description: Path to the file to write
